Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ১) A full tank gets emptied in 8 minutes due to the presence of a leak in it. On opening a tap which can fill the tank at the rate of 9 L/min, the tank gets emptied in 12 min. Find the capacity of a tank?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
a = 8; b = 9; C = 12
Capacity of a tank
= a × b × c/(c-a)
= (8 × 9 × 12)/4
= 216 Litre.

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ২) If a pipe A can fill a tank 3 times faster than pipe B. If both the pipes can fill the tank in 32 minutes, then the slower pipe alone will be able to fill the tank in?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
Time is taken by pipe A = x
Time is taken by pipe B = x/3
1/x + 3/x = 1/32
x = 128 minutes

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ৩) Pipe A is 4 times as fast as B in filling a tank. If A takes 20 minutes to fill a tank, then what is the time taken by both the pipe A and B to fill the tank?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
A takes 20 minutes and it is 4 times faster than B,
it means B will take 80 minutes to fill the tank.
(1/20 + 1/80) × t = 1.
So, We get t = 16.

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ৪) A and B can together finish a work 30 days. They worked together for 20 days and then B left. After another 20 days, A finished the remaining work. In how many days A alone can finish the work?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
(A +B)'s 20 day's work = 20 × 1/30 = 2/3
Remaining work = 1 − 2/3 = 1/3
Now,1/ 3 work is done by A in 20 days
∴ The whole work will be done by A
in 20×3 = 60days

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ৫) A and B completed a work together in 5 days. Had A worked at twice the speed and B at half the speed, it would have taken them four days to complete the job. How much time would it take for A alone to do the work?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
Assume work to be done 100%.
First case,
A + B = 100/5 = 20% work done per day -------- (1)
Second case,
2A + B/2 = 100/4 = 25% work done per day ------ (2)
On solving equation (1) and (2), we get
A = 10 days

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ৬) A boy and girl together fill a cistern with water. The boy pours 4 liters of water every 3 minutes and the girl pours 3 litres every 4 minutes. How much time will it take to fill 100 litres of water in the cistern?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
Water filled by (boy + girl) in one minute,
4/3 + 3/4
= (16+9)/12
= 25/12 liter
Hence, time taken to fill 100 liter,
= (100 × 12)/25
= 48 minutes

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ৭) Pipe A can fill the tank in 8 hours and pipe B can fill it in 12 hours. If pipe A is opened at 7:00 AM and pipe B is opened at 9:00 AM, then at what time will the tank be full ?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
A opened 2 hours early to B
In 2 hours A can do 3 × 2 = 6 unit work
Remaining work = 24 - 6 = 18
A + B can do it in
= 18/5 hours
= 3 hours 36 minutes
∴ Tank will be full in 9 A.M. + 3 hours 36 minutes = 12.36 P.M.

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ৮) Two pipes A and B can fill a water tank in 20 and 24 minutes respectively and a third pipe C can empty at the rate of 3 gallons per minute. If A, B and C are open together to fill the tank in 15 minutes, find the capacity of the tank?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
Work done by the C pipe in 1 minute
= 1/15 − (1/20 + 1/24)
= (1/15 − 11/120)
= −1/40 [−ve means emptying]
∴ Volume of 1/ 40 part = 3 gallons.
Volume of whole = (3 × 40) gallons = 120 gallons.

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ৯) 3/ 4 part of the tank is full of water. When 30 litres of water is taken out, the tank becomes empty. The capacity of the tank is -
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
If a tank has 4x liters of total capacity and it holds 3x liters of water and if 30 liters of water is taken out, the tank becomes empty.
It means 3x liters of water is taken out
3x = 30 liters
x = 10 liters
Capacity of tank
= 4x = 4 × 10 = 40 liters

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ১০) A pipe can fill a tank in x hours and another pipe can empty it in y (y > x) hours. If both pipes are open, in how many hours will the tank is filled?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
Net part filled in 1 hour
= (1/x − 1/y)
= (y−x)/xy
∴ The tank will be filled in
= xy/(y−x) hours

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ১১) 12 pumps working 6 hours a day can empty a completely filled reservoir in 15 days. How many such pumps working 9 hours a day will empty the same reservoir in 12 days?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
Apply formula of
M1D1H1/W1= M2D2H2/W2
Let 'P' pumps are required to empty the reservoir.
(12pumps×6hours×15days)/1 reservoir
= (P×9hours×12days)/1 reservoir
P = 10 pumps

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ১২) Two pipes A and B together can fill a cistern in 4 hours. Had they been opened separately, then B would have taken 6 hours more than A to fill the cistern. How much time will be taken by A to fill the cistern separately?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
Let the cistern be filled by pipe A alone in x hours.
Then, pipe B will fill it in (x + 6) hours
∴ 1/ x + 1/ x+6 = 1/ 4
⇒ x+6+x/ x(x+6) = 1/ 4
⇒ x² − 2x−24 = 0
⇒ (x−6)(x+4) = 0
⇒ x = 6 [neglecting the negative value of x].

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ১৩) A tank is filled in 5 hours by three pipes A, B and C. The pipe C is twice as fast as B and B is twice as fast as A. How much time will pipe A alone take to fill the tank?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
Suppose pipe A alone takes x hours to fill the tank.
Then, pipes B and C will take x/2 and x/4 hours respectively to fill the tank.
∴ 1/x + 2/x + 4/x = 1/5
⇒ 7/x = 1/5
⇒ x = 35 hours

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ১৪) Three pipes A, B and C can fill a tank from empty to full in 30 minutes, 20 minutes, and 10 minutes respectively. When the tank is empty, all the three pipes are opened. A, B and C discharge chemical solutions P, Q and R respectively. What is the proportion of the solution R in the liquid in the tank after 3 minutes?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
Part filled by (A + B + C) in 3 minutes
= 3(1/30 + 1/20 + 1/10)
= 3 × 11/60
= 11/20
Part filled by C in 3 minutes = 3/10
∴ Required ratio
= 3/10 × 20/11
= 6/11

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ১৫) Having the same capacity 9 taps fill up a water tank in 20 minutes. How many taps of the same capacity are required to fill up the same water tank in 15 minutes?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
(m1×h1×t1)/w1 = (m2×h2×t2)/w2
9 taps × 20 min = t taps × 15 min
So, t = 12 taps

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ১৬) A, B and C completed a work costing Tk. 1800. A worked for 6 days, B for 4 days and C for 9 days. If their daily wages are in the ratio of 5 : 6 : 4, how much amount will be received by A?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
Let the daily wages of A, B and C be Tk. 5x, Tk. 6x and Tk. 4x respectively.
Then, ratio of their amounts
= (5×6):(6×4):(4x9)
= 30:24:36
= 5:4:6
∴ A's amount
= Tk. (1800 × 5/15)
= Tk. 600

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ১৭) A group of men decided to do a job in 4 days. But since 20 men drop out every day, the job is completed at the end of the 7th day. How many men were there at the beginning?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
Let X be the initial number of men then,
According to the question,
4X = X + (X - 20) + (X - 40) + (X - 60) + (X - 80) + (X - 100) + (X - 120)
⇒ 4X = 7X - 420
⇒ 3X = 420
⇒ X = 420/3
⇒ X = 140 men

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ১৮) A can finish a piece of work in 18 days and B can do the same work in half of the time taken by A. Then working together what part of the same work they can finish in a day?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
A's 1 day work = 1/18
B's 1 day work = 1/9 [because B take half time than A]
So, (A + B)'s one day work
= 1/18 + 1/9
= (1+2)/18
= 1/6

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ১৯) Two men can do a piece of work in x days. But y women can do that in 3 days. Then the ratio of the work done by 1 man and 1 woman is?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
2 men can do a work in x days
1 men can do a work in (2 × x) days
y women can do a work in 3 days
1 women can do a work in 3y days
1 man : 1 woman
Days - 2x : 3y
Efficiency - 3y : 2x

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ২০) 10 men working 6 hours a day can complete a work in 18 days. How many hours a day must 15 men work to complete the same work in 12 days?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
(10 men × 6 hours × 18 days)/1work = (15 men × 12 days × H hour/day)/1work
⇒ 6 hours/day

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ২১) A and B can do a work in 8 days, B and C can do the same work in 12 days. A, B and C together can finish it in 6 days. A and C together will do it in = ?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
(A+B+C)'s 1 day's work = 1/6
(A+B)'s 1 day's work = 1/8
(B+C)'s 1 day's work = 1/12
∴ (A+C)'s 1 day's work
= (2× 1/6) − (1/8 + 1/12)
= (1/3 − 5/24)
= 3/24
= 1/8
So, A and C together will do the work in 8 days.

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ২২) 3 men or 5 women can do a work in 12 days. How long will 6 men and 5 women take to finish the work?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
According to the question,
3 men = 5 women
As they complete the same work in same time
6 men + 5 women
= 6 men + 3 men
= 9 men
If, 3 men does a work in 12 days
1 men does a work in 12 × 3
9 men does a work in (12×3)/9
= 4 days

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ২৩) The ratio of the amount of work done by (x-1) labours in (x+1) days and (x+1) labours in (x+2) days is 5 : 6. Then the value of x is?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
From M1D1 = M2D2
⇒ M1D1 / M2D2 = 5/6
⇒ (x−1)(x+1)/(x+1)(x+2) = 5/6
⇒ (x−1)/(x+2) = 5/6
⇒ 6x−6 = 5x+10
⇒ x = 16

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ২৪) 639 persons can repair a road in 12 days working 5 hours a day. In how many days will 30 persons working 6 hours a day complete the work ?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
According to the question,
Let, D is number of days
(639×12×5)/1 road = (30×6×D)/1 road
⇒ D = 213 days

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ২৫) A and B together can complete a work in 12 days. B and C together can complete the same work in 8 days and A and C together can complete it in 16 days. In total, how many days do A, B and C together take to complete the same work ?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
(A+B)'s 1 day's work = 1/12
(B+C)'s 1 day's work = 1/8
(A+C)'s 1 day's work = 1/16
Adding, we get 2(A + B + C)'s 1 day's work
= (1/12 + 1/8 + 1/16)
= (18/144)+(12/144)+(9/144)
= (39/144) or (13/48)th of the work in a day.
Or A, B and C do (13/96)th of the work in a day.
So, A, B and C together can complete the work in = 96/13 days

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ২৬) A can finish a work in 18 days and B can do the same work in 15 days. B worked for 10 days and left the job. In how many days, A alone can finish the remaining work?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
B's 10day's work = 1/15 × 10 = 2/3
Remaining work =
(1−2)/3 = 1/3
Now,
1/18 work is done by A in 1 day
∴ 1/3 work is done by A in 18 × 1/3 = 6 days

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ২৭) To complete a work, A takes 50% more time than B. If together they take 18 days to complete the work, how much time shall B take to do it?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
We have B = 3/2 × A
→ A = 2/3 × B
One day's work,
A+B = 1/18
2/3×B+B = 1/18
5/3×B = 1/18
Oneday's work of B = 3/90
B alone can complete the work in = 90/3 = 30days

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ২৮) Working 5 hours a day, A can complete a work in 8 days and working 6 hours a day, B can complete the same work in 10 days. Working 8 hours a day, they can jointly complete the work in:
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
Working 5 hours a day, A can complete the work in 8 days i.e.
= 5 × 8 = 40 hours
Working 6 hours a day, B can complete the work in 10 days i.e.
= 6 × 10 = 60 hours
(A + B)'s 1 hour's work,
= 1/40 + 1/60 = (3+2)/ 120
= 5/120
= 1/24
Hence, A and B can complete the work in 24 hours i.e. they require 3 days to complete the work.

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ২৯) A and B together can complete a work in 3 days. They started together but after 2 days, B left the work. If the work is completed after two more days, B alone could do the work in-
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
(A+B)'s one day's work = 1/3 part
(A+B) works 2 days together = 2/3 part
Remaining work = (1−2)/3 = 1/3 part
1/3 part of work is completed by A in two days
Hence, one day's work of A = 1/6
Then, one day's work of B = 1/3 − 1/6 = 1/6
So, B alone can complete the whole work in 6 days.

Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.question: ৩০) If A and B together can complete a piece of work in 15 days and B alone in 20 days, in how many days can A alone complete the work?
Time & Work, Pipes & Cisterns.exp:
A and B complete a work in = 15 days
One day's work of (A + B) = 1/15
B complete the work in = 20 days
One day's work of B = 1/ 20
Then, A's one day's work
= 1/15 − 1/20
= (4−3)/60
= 1/60
Thus, A can complete the work in = 60 days.
